content: Lets build a simple desk gadget ! which will display time and weather.

Thanks for the warm intro — and good news: I can see from your maker profile that you're already set up for this kind of project. You've got a 0.96" OLED screen, an ESP32, and even a 3D printer, which is basically a dream starter kit for a tiny time + weather display.

Before I write any plans, I want to understand your vision so we build *your* gadget, not a generic one. A few simple questions — no tech jargon, just tell me what feels right:

<questions>
[
  {
    "id": "purpose",
    "text": "What will this gadget be for, mostly?",
    "type": "single_select",
    "options": [
      "A nice piece for my own desk, something I'll look at every day",
      "A gift for someone (family, friend, coworker)",
      "A fun weekend build to learn and tinker",
      "A demo / portfolio piece to show off my skills"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "weather_source",
    "text": "When you say 'weather', what do you actually want to see?",
    "type": "single_select",
    "options": [
      "The weather outside my window (needs internet)",
      "The temperature & humidity of my room (measured locally)",
      "Both - outside weather AND my room's conditions",
      "I'm not sure - what's easiest?"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "extra_info",
    "text": "Besides the time, what else would be nice to glance at?",
    "type": "multi_select",
    "options": [
      "Date and day of the week",
      "Temperature (and maybe a little icon: sun, cloud, rain)",
      "A tiny alarm or reminder",
      "Nothing else - keep it super minimal"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "look",
    "text": "How do you picture it looking on the desk?",
    "type": "single_select",
    "options": [
      "Small and cute - like a little standing card or cube",
      "A classic mini clock - face angled toward me",
      "Sleek and modern - maybe a minimalist slab",
      "Whatever looks coolest with the 3D printer"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "power",
    "text": "How do you want to power it?",
    "type": "single_select",
    "options": [
      "Plugged in with a USB cable - always on",
      "Battery powered - no visible wires",
      "Either is fine - you pick what's simpler"
    ]
  },
  {
    "id": "budget",
    "text": "Do you want to buy any new parts, or stick to what's already in your drawer?",
    "type": "single_select",
    "options": [
      "Use only what I already have",
      "I'm fine spending a little for something nicer",
      "Surprise me - just keep it cheap"
    ]
  }
]
</questions>

Take your time — you can also just type answers in plain words if that's easier. Once I know how you see it, I'll write up a proper plan (what it does, what it costs, and the simplest version we can build first).
reasoning:
Both existing projects are basically stubs - they have AGENTS.md, stage.json, and messages.jsonl but no actual context/ files. These look like previous attempts that never really got going.

The user's request: "Lets build a simple desk gadget ! which will display time and weather."

This is fresh. I'm the Project Architect. My job per the system prompt: engage in warm, collaborative dialogue, ask simple layman questions via <questions> block (no CLI tools). Once vision is clear, write context/context.md, context/prd.md, context/mvp.md.

I should note their profile already tells me a lot:
- Intermediate skill
- ESP32 / Pico available
- Has 0.96" I2C OLED (SSD1306), DHT22, SG90 servos
- USB-C / LiPo power
- Arduino C++ / PlatformIO
- Has 3D printer

Given they have an OLED and this is a time+weather display, they probably don't even need new components — ESP32 + OLED over WiFi for weather, or Pico with DHT22 for local temp/humidity. But I shouldn't assume — I should ask questions. Keep it simple, layman, encouraging.

Let me ask a small batch of questions. Not too many — maybe 4-5 key ones:
1. Where will it sit / how will you use it (desk, nightstand, gift)?
2. What should "weather" mean to them — outside weather from internet, or room temp/humidity measured locally, or both?
3. Do they want it to show more than time (date, day, weather icon, temp)?
4. Size/style preference — small puck, portrait, landscape?
5. Power — always plugged in via USB, or battery?
6. Budget rough?

I should keep them warm and layman. Use the <questions> block as required. Let me greet them warmly first, mention what I know from the profile, then ask.

I'll craft the questions with the required XML-ish block. Format: <questions>[{...}]</questions>. The system prompt example shows it inline. I'll follow exactly that format.

Keep it to about 6 questions max so it's not overwhelming.
